newsitem.title: USA: Russia mulls over bank depositors insurance.
newsitem.headline: Russia mulls over bank depositors insurance.

text.p: Russia is considering establishing some form of depositors insurance to enhance confidence in its banks, many of which are in shaky condition, said Denis Kiselyov, director of banking supervision at Bank of Russia.
"We have been studying the possibility of depositors insurance," Kiselyov said in a Reuters interview on Thursday. "The problem is the cost."

The government presently has no funds and most of the banks are unwilling to share the cost, he said, adding that assistance from multilateral agencies, such as the International Monetary Fund, or the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development would likely fall short of the amount needed.
In Russia, 90 percent of the deposits are controlled in 10 percent of the 2,200 banks, he said.
Deposit-taking has not been a major activity for the hundreds of the new banks that sprang up in the past six years.
Kiselyov estimated that more than half of the revenues of many Russian banks were derived from speculation in foreign exchange and government securities.
Kiselyov told a banking conference organized by Arther Andersen consulting that shrinking profits from speculation may force many undercapitalized Russian banks to merge or to go out of business.
Some 400 to 500 Russian banks have zero or negative capital on their books, he said at the conference.
